text: DeltaServe retains host-engine queueing, batching, KV-cache, sampling, and forward execution while intercepting scheduled batches to add synthetic prefill-only fine-tuning rows.
A paper-faithful DeltaServe backend needs residual-stream activation capture and a separate CUDA MPS backward process using shared GPU memory.
DeltaServe admission is SLO-driven, shortest-sample-first, activation-capacity-aware, and graph-versus-eager latency aware.

DeltaServe targets bounded interference and SLO compliance, not literally zero interference; the paper reports nonzero inference overhead including about 22 percent average latency increase in one light workload.
vLLM supports a custom scheduler class but warns that its scheduler interface is not public and compatibility is not guaranteed.
The standard vLLM 0.21.0 model runner executes under torch inference_mode and therefore does not retain the autograd graph required for fine-tuning backward.
The WSL environment runs vLLM 0.21.0 and Qwen3-0.6B on the RTX 5070 Ti, and all four dependency-free admission-core tests pass.
The current vLLM adapter fails because pooling_params is missing, vanilla EngineCore lacks register_deltaserve_hooks, and execute_model is wrapped in inference_mode.
The local Qwen3-0.6B benchmark measured CUDA-graph throughput 4.57 times eager throughput at batch one and 2.31 times eager throughput at batch four.
The tested WSL environment lacks NVIDIA MPS executables and its spawned PyTorch CUDA IPC tensor transfer fails with invalid resource handle.
The current activation buffer is token accounting rather than tensor storage, and backward is only controller state rather than loss, autograd, optimizer, or adapter update execution.
The CLIF DeltaServe bridge is not wired into the existing launcher or replica path, which still uses model.generate and local_train.
The prototype is approximately 15 to 20 percent complete as an engineering scaffold but zero percent complete as an end-to-end concurrent training-and-inference demonstration.
The next implementation milestone should first make a real single-process vLLM mixed-forward path work, then add activation-backed backward, and only then pursue MPS and CUDA IPC isolation.
